verdict.reasoning: Patient describes a severe headache for a few days that is worsening: "really crazy headache that's been going on for a few days" and rates it 8/10; later confirms it has been getting worse over the last three days.
Duration and severity are documented: "Around three days ago, maybe" and pain rated as "probably an 8."
Location is described as diffuse but mainly right periorbital: "it kind of feels all over my head, but like mainly around my right eye."
Character is described as dull with occasional sharpness: "It's kind of. It's dull, but sometimes it gets a bit sharper."
Gradual onset is stated: "So basically it like it developed gradually, I guess."
Headache is constant with fluctuating intensity: "it kind of comes and goes, but I mean, it is there all the time, but like sometimes it's stronger."
Severity rating given: when asked 1–10, patient says "It's probably an 8."
Photophobia described: patient notes light is annoying and painful—"now like light is quite annoying my eyes" and when asked "does it hurt to look at bright lights?" replies "Yeah, yeah, it hurts."
Visual phenomena are reported: "just when it started I got this like weird shooting lights."

The note claims associated nausea, but transcript clarifies: Doctor: "Any nausea or any vomiting?" Patient: "Well, basically I'm sick with the headache, but I. No vomiting." The patient does not explicitly confirm nausea; "sick with the headache" is ambiguous and nausea is neither clearly affirmed nor denied.
Vomiting is denied: Doctor: "Any nausea or any vomiting?" Patient: "Well, basically I'm sick with the headache, but I. No vomiting."
Fever denied: Doctor: "Any temperatures or fevers?" Patient: "No."
Neck stiffness denied: Doctor: "Any neck pain or neck stiffness?" Patient: "No."
Focal weakness denied: Doctor: "Any difficulty with weakness in your arms and legs?" Patient: "No."
Speech disturbance denied: Doctor: "Any difficulty with speaking or speech?" Patient: "No."
Ibuprofen use and frequency documented: Patient: "So I tried ibuprofen. So I took like a few for the last two days" and later clarifies "Three a day." Effect: "But it doesn't really help."
Past response to ibuprofen described: "Yeah, I mean, I had, but usually after I take ibuprofen, it kind of goes away, so. But this time it's just not."

No other history provided; when asked "Do you have any other medical history?" patient replies "I think so. It's just a headache." No surgical history is mentioned anywhere, so absence of documented PMH/PSH is accurate.
No regular meds: Doctor: "do you take any regular medication?" Patient: "No."
Recent ibuprofen use stated: "So I tried ibuprofen. So I took like a few for the last two days, basically."
No known drug allergies: Doctor: "Do you have any allergies to any medications?" Patient: "Not that I know of."
Mother’s migraines described as more severe: "my mom's is like quite bad... it... takes her out for a few days, basically."
Sister has migraines: Patient: "my sister and my mum have them quite frequently"; later: "my sister's like, better. Like it kind of is very rare."
Work and screen use: Patient: "I work in it, so I work with computers a lot."
Living situation: Patient: "I live with housemates, so three of them."
Glasses and lack of recent eye test: Doctor: "Do you wear glasses?" Patient: "Yes, I do." Doctor: "Have you had a recent eye check done?" Patient: "No, I've been wearing them since I was five."
Social smoking and alcohol: Doctor: "do you drink or smoke at all?" Patient: "I socially smoke and I drink. Not only socially." Doctor clarifies: "Only socially. Okay."
Recent work stress: Doctor asks about stress; Patient: "Well, it's been a bit stressful kicking off a new project, but yeah, nothing out of the ordinary really."

Doctor’s assessment: "I do think this could be a headache very similar to migraine... Given your mum and your sister also have migraines." Headache is 3 days, progressive, with photophobia (light hurts), visual aura-like "shooting lights," poor ibuprofen response, and family history—matching a likely migraine phenotype.
Functional impairment at work: Patient: "It's hard to focus though, so I had to take a couple of days off work actually."

Codeine-containing analgesic prescribed: Doctor: "we can also add in other painkillers like paracetamol or codeine" and later: "I can give you a prescription for that today" after patient mentions codeine.
Naproxen discussed: Doctor: "Or I can prescribe you something stronger like naproxen, which is another anti inflammatory, which can be helpful."
Paracetamol mentioned as option: Doctor: "We can also add in other painkillers like paracetamol or codeine, which might be helpful as well."
Ibuprofen dosing advice: "You try the ibuprofen. Now, my only worry is I'm not sure whether you're taking the correct dose. You can take up to two tablets three times a day."
Reducing screen brightness is mentioned as something the patient already did: "I had to like reduce the brightness of my screen." The doctor does not advise this as part of the plan.
Advice on repeat eye exam: Doctor: "if you feel like your eyes are straining, I would always recommend having a repeat eye test done."
Headache diary recommendation: "With regards to the next few days, it may be worth keeping a headache diary so we can try and work out what's... If there's any triggers."

Follow-up 1–2 weeks with possible prophylaxis: "I'd like you to come back and see me in about a week's time. Week to two weeks time. If you are having more frequent episodes... we can think about giving you medications as prophylactic."

Safety netting given: Doctor advises to return or call if headaches worsen or not better, and specifically if "any problems with your vision or weakness in your arms and legs, or you're just not feeling very well, just give me a call and come back and see me."
Transcript contains no vital signs, physical examination findings, or diagnostic tests; only history and plan are discussed.

Follow-up plan: "I'd like you to come back and see me in about a week's time. Week to two weeks time. If you are having more frequent episodes... we can think about giving you medications as prophylactic."
